Nuri is operated by Nurisoft Development OÜ, Tallinn, Estonia. Self-custody describes the crypto wallet, not card or bank balances. Card and banking services are provided by regulated third-party providers and are subject to separate eligibility, verification and terms.

Current payment rails.

Nuri’s public site currently describes SEPA and USD ACH transfers, Visa card access, Apple Pay / Google Pay, and M-PESA / other mobile-money routes where available.

Card & Bank Support →

Simple outside. Deeper underneath.

The current public About page describes a passkey-based self-custodial wallet with co-signing. The deeper product architecture can expose multisig, independent recovery, hardware security keys and open recovery tooling without making those concepts part of the first-run experience.

Current About page →

Wallet first. Services second.

The core trust boundary is explicit: the self-custodial wallet is separate from optional card and banking balances. Connected financial providers can have their own availability, compliance and counterparty risks; they do not become the custody layer for the user’s self-custodial wallet.

Wirex and regulated services.

Nuri’s Card & Bank Support page states that Nuri Card is issued on Wirex BaaS.

  • UK: Wirex Limited is authorised and regulated by the FCA as an electronic money institution.
  • EEA card services use regulated programme entities including Transact Payments Malta Limited.
  • SEPA and ACH availability depends on country and account eligibility.
